item.title: Packers’ Evan Williams reflects on incredible connection between his mom and Tom Brady
item.description: Mandatory Credit: David Butler II-Imagn Images Packers’ Evan Williams reflects on incredible connection between his mom and Tom Brady appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Green Bay Packers laid a massive 45-27 beatdown on the New England Patriots on Fox, with Pats great Tom Brady on commentary. During the broadcast, it was revealed that Packers safety Evan Williams’ mother, Dani, who was at the game, had actually babysat Brady when he was around five years old. After the game, Williams was asked about that remarkable fact. He gave a bit of backstory about her mom growing up in the Bay Area, where Brady was also from. His grandfather and Brady’s father had apparently played together. He also recalled how casually she told her that she had babysat the GOAT . “I remember her telling me when I was growing up, I was probably starting high school or something, and she just tossed it out, ‘Oh yeah, I babysat Tom Brady, by the way,’ and then continues another conversation. ‘Like woah, woah, woah! We gotta go back!’ I never was really too sure, but apparently it’s true,” Williams said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) It turned out to be a great day for Williams and the Green Bay defense. Williams picked off Drake Maye, one of three Packers interceptions in the game. It was also Williams’ third INT of the season, putting him level with Xavier McKinney for the team lead. The Packers defenders have become absolute ballhawks under first-year defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon. They now have 13 interceptions on the season, which leads the league. If they can continue to force turnovers at that rate with Jordan Love playing like a potential MVP , they will be a very dangerous team moving forward. Related: Packers QB Jordan Love reacts to MVP chants at place nearly 2,000 miles away from Lambeau Related: Packers’ Matt LaFleur reveals tricky Josh Jacobs injury after Patriots clash

item.title: UCF prevails in yet another off-the-rails finish, defeating Kansas, 33-32
item.description: LAWRENCE, KANSAS - NOVEMBER 07: Running back Taevion Swint #4 of the UCF Knights celebrates a touchdown run with teammates against the Kansas Jayhawks in the second half at David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Lawrence, Kansas. (Photo by Ed Zurga/Getty Images) | Getty Images UCF and chaotic, seemingly inexplicable finishes have become quite the pairing this season. Two weeks after knocking off BYU in perhaps the wildest ending of the college football season , the Knights found themselves in another crunch time thriller Saturday, this time on the road at Kansas. For most of the contest, UCF appeared on track to secure its first comfortable victory in Big 12 play. The Knights built a 26-7 lead by the 9:52 mark of the third quarter, seemingly having solved the Jayhawks on both sides of the ball. But their next two possessions went nowhere, producing consecutive three-and-outs that combined for -6 yards. That sudden offensive futility left the door ajar for a Kansas comeback, and the Jayhawks capitalized with two-straight touchdown drives and a field goal to trim the deficit to 26-24. Then, following a spectacular punt by Atticus Bertrams, Kansas regained possession at its own 5-yard line with 2:27 remaining, needing just a field goal to complete the program’s largest comeback since 2010. Somehow, the Jayhawks crammed 11 plays and 95 yards into 81 seconds, capping the clutch drive with a Dylan Edwards touchdown run with 1:06 remaining, catapulting Kansas ahead 32-26. But the scoring drive was so quick that it granted UCF 66 seconds of opportunity while armed with two timeouts. The drive did not start in promising fashion as the Knights opened the drive with several misfires. But quarterback Alonza Barnett III — making his first start since suffering a hamstring injury in Week 2 — caught fire, jumpstarting the offense with a 20-yard completion to Tyren Hornes on 3rd-and-10. Then he hit Chase Hinshaw for another 20 and Josh Derry for a 19-yar pickup, positioning UCF 15 yards away from the end zone with 13 seconds remaining. Then, the Knights went for the punishing blow. Barnett lofted a pass toward the back of the end zone, where Derry made a juggling grab while falling backward. The official initially threw his hands up to signal touchdown, but the replay review showed Derry had not secured possession before landing out of bounds. The call was overturned, leaving UCF eight seconds to work with. The next attempt didn’t produce a touchdown, but it still benefited the Knights. They drew a pass interference penalty, advancing the ball from the 15-yard line to the 6, giving UCF one more opportunity to reclaim the victory. On the deciding play, Barnett kept his eyes to the left from the snap, patiently waiting for tight end Caden Piening to break toward the boundary. Barnett fired the pass, and Piening made a diving catch right before the sideline. The official emphatically raised both arms to the sky to signal a UCF touchdown, but on

item.title: NFC Playoff Picture update: Seahawks remain outside of final Wild Card spot despite win
item.description: The Seattle Seahawks got the win they needed against the Arizona Cardinals, but they didn’t exactly get favorable results elsewhere in the NFC standings. As expected, the San Francisco 49ers dispatched the Las Vegas Raiders to temporarily assume control of the No. 1 seed again. While the NFC South tripped over itself like usual (except the New Orleans Saints), the NFC North was a perfect 3-0 on Sunday, with the Chicago Bears overcoming five turnovers to beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on a last-second field goal. Probably one of the biggest results of the day was the Green Bay Packers hammering the New England Patriots in a 45-27 romp, which is the result that currently keeps the Seahawks out of a playoff spot. NFC playoff standings entering Monday night 1. San Francisco 49ers (7-1) 2. Minnesota Vikings (6-1) – Monday Night Football vs. Buffalo Bills pending 3. New York Giants (5-2-1) 4. Carolina Panthers (3-5, 1-1 NFCS) 5. Chicago Bears (7-2) 6. Detroit Lions (6-2) 7. Green Bay Packers (6-3) 8. Seattle Seahawks (5-4, 2-1 NFCW) 9. Los Angeles Rams (5-4, 0-2 NFCW) 10. Dallas Cowboys (4-5) 11. New Orleans Saints (3-5) 12. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6, win over ATL, 3-3 NFC) 13. Atlanta Falcons (3-6, loss to TB, 3-3 NFC) 14. Arizona Cardinals (3-6, 2-5 NFC) 15. Washington Commanders (2-5-1) 16. Philadelphia Eagles (2-7) If we’re being honest with ourselves, the NFC West title is on the cusp of being out of reach, and would be nailed on out of reach with a loss to the 49ers in Week 12. Even outside of the division race, the Seahawks’ Wild Card hopes rest on overtaking one of these red-hot NFC North teams and fending off the resurgent Rams, who’ve won three straight. It might be a bad thing if the Bears get dragged into the WC race given the head-to-head tiebreaker on Chicago, so a Bears NFC North title might be preferred in the long run. There’s a good chance that 10 wins might not be enough to get a Wild Card spot. Six wins might be enough to win the NFC South, but the Seahawks don’t play in that division, unfortunately.

item.title: On the future of the NBA in Mexico, from the Global Games to a franchise
item.description: MEXICO CITY: No city outside the United States or Canada has hosted more regular season NBA games than Mexico City. So it should come as no surprise that the annual tilts held in the Mexican capital are the frequent backdrop for rumbles about the league setting up shop on a more permanent basis in the largest metropolis on the continent. In recent years, however, the league making a return to the Pacific Northwest to put a new team back in Seattle, Washington along with a new team in Las Vegas, Nevada seemed a fait accompli, and with it, hope for an NBA team in the city faded. But before the start of the 2026 season, it was announced at an NBA Board of Governor's meeting that Mexico City was back in the mix with a potential ownership group and arena district lined up. Still, the Mexico City Game has been and will likely remain the gem in the crown of the league that is their Global Games series, a yearly accomplishment on its own signifying the nascent talent and fandom of Latin America now percolating into the league's ranks. To learn more, the Rookie Wire caught up with NBA Latin America and Canada Head of Operations Raul Zarraga ahead of the 2026 Mexico City Game between the Denver Nuggets and Indiana Pacers . From the state of the Association in Mexico, and what the future of Mexico City Games and NBA expansion in the region might look like, our conversation covered the gamut and then some. This interview has been lightly edited for the purposes of clarity and brevity. Rookie Wire: What it is you do with regard to the Mexico City games? Raul Zarraga : Of course. The Global Game – it's a great opportunity for us. You have this life experience for fans and partners and everyone in the community, and all the people enjoying the game. Keep in mind that less than one percent of people around the world have the opportunity to be in-person for a regular season NBA game. And that's why it's very important for us to give a piece of that action to all the fans in Mexico. I wish we could have many more games available for fans. But we are very happy with the experience so far. It's sold out in a couple of days. The two amazing teams, we're really looking forward to (having them) here: the Pacers and the Nuggets. The Pacers for the first time, the Nuggets the second, and it's a whole celebration together, a unique way to mix two very important components: entertainment and the culture. Something that the fans are really looking for, regardless if they are core, casual, (or) curious fans of our 30 million fans (in Latin America), this is a great opportunity to enjoy the NBA. And we have other assets at the Capitanes (Mexico City's G League team) as well for live experiences. So we have this regular season (game), and then we tip off the season for Capitanes for 21 games of regular season happening here. So, it's a great momentum for players, for legends, for the fans, for the community, for the partners, for the people watching the game through the differ

item.title: Best division ever? How NFC North is on pace to make history in 2026
item.description: Best division ever? How NFC North is on pace to make history in 2026 originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Bears found a way to win on Sunday night, overcoming five turnovers to defeat the Buccaneers 27-24, but they certainly aren't alone in the NFC North. The Packers and Lions both continued their winning ways on Sunday, and, until Monday at least, none of those three teams can say they only one loss like the Vikings do. All four NFC North teams will enter Week 10 in the playoff picture. While head-to-head matchups might hurt the division's chances of getting every team into the playoffs, it's becoming clear these four teams are in a class of their own as a group. Here's a look at how the NFC North could be headed for uncharted territory. MORE: Which NFL trade candidates boosted - or hurt - their stocks in Week 9? NFC North combined record The NFC North is now 25-8 (.757) through nearly nine weeks, with five of those eight losses simply coming against one another. NFC North teams are 20-3 in non-divisional games. Here are the standings after Sunday night, with the Vikings still to play on Monday: Team Record Pct. Vikings 6-1 .857 Bears 7-2 .778 Lions 6-2 .750 Packers 6-3 .667 Every team in the division is at least three games over .500, meaning the Packers are in last place at 6-3. In the NFC North, for comparison, the 3-5 Panthers lead the division. The Bears have had a hard time gaining ground during the four-game win streak because of all of the success around them, but a Vikings loss to the Bills on Monday night would rocket Chicago into first place. MORE: 4 quarterbacks who boosted their early MVP cases in Week 9 Best division in NFL history When it comes to divisions, there are two distinct periods in the NFL: pre-2002, when divisions were larger than four teams, and 2002-present, when all divisions have been comprised of four teams. The overall records within divisions were more even before 2002 because more teams were in each. Since 2002, the best record for a division belongs to the 2024 NFC North, which saw teams go a combined 45-23 (.662) as the Lions went 15-2, Vikings went 14-3, Packers went 11-6 and Bears went 7-10. Two years earlier, in the NFC East went a combined 43-23-2, sending three teams to the playoffs. So far, the NFC North is on track to break its own record in 2026. At 25-8 (.757), every team is at least three games above .500 and their combined record would have to be 20-15 the rest of the way to match the 2024 mark. There are still seven divisional games on the docket in the NFC North, so the division will have at least 15 losses. If these four teams can keep it to only eight additional losses, the division will tie its own record from 2002. item.title: Browns’ Shedeur Sanders reflects on notable moments vs. Saints despite loss
item.description: Matthew Hinton-Imagn Images Browns’ Shedeur Sanders reflects on notable moments vs. Saints despite loss appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Shedeur Sanders did not get the result he wanted in his first start of the 2026 NFL season. However, the Cleveland Browns quarterback showed plenty of fight in a heartbreaking 23-22 overtime loss to the New Orleans Saints. Thrust into action after Deshaun Watson entered concussion protocol, Sanders navigated a difficult afternoon at Caesars Superdome. He delivered a fourth-quarter rally and answered New Orleans’ overtime touchdown before Cleveland’s failed two-point conversion ended the comeback attempt. Despite being sacked five times, Sanders remained composed when the pressure intensified. After the game, he credited the Browns’ coaching staff and quarterback room for preparing him. #Browns QB Shedeur Sanders on being able to come up with some clutch moments as the game went on: Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) "Deshaun did a great job this whole year leading the team. Unfortunately, he wasn't able to play today, and I had to step in and get the rhythm of the team and get the feeling, get… pic.twitter.com/orxaj227Af — Camryn Justice (@camijustice) November 8, 2026 “Deshaun did a great job this whole year leading the team. Unfortunately, he wasn’t able to play today, and I had to step in and get the rhythm of the team and get the feeling, get everything back,” Sanders said, via News 5 Cleveland’s Camryn Justice. He also thanked the organization for giving him valuable practice opportunities. He also acknowledged the contributions of his fellow quarterbacks throughout the week. Sanders emphasized that the performance was a collective effort rather than an individual achievement. “Everything was good. I was excited for it. It was a team effort, I would say, and it’s just when the pressure is on, it’s just time to shine,” he added. Sanders’ 2026 campaign had largely been spent waiting behind Watson. He has had limited opportunities to see the field. Sunday’s start, however, offered an important glimpse of his potential under pressure. The Browns ultimately left New Orleans with a painful defeat. That said, Sanders gave head coach Todd Monken another reason to trust the depth of his quarterback room. Cleveland now turns its attention to a Week 10 matchup against Houston. Related: Browns’ Todd Monken drops mic on mentality behind going for 2 to win in OT Related: Browns’ Todd Monken doesn’t want to talk about Shedeur Sanders vs. Deshaun Watson yet after heartbreaking loss

item.title: Devils’ Connor Hellebuyck reacts to shocking benching in Jets homecoming
item.description: John Jones-Imagn Images Devils’ Connor Hellebuyck reacts to shocking benching in Jets homecoming appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New Jersey Devils are not playing Connor Hellebuyck against the Winnipeg Jets on Tuesday night. The Devils traded for Hellebuyck last month in a blockbuster deal with the Jets. However, he won’t face his former team when New Jersey travels to the Canada Life Centre for Tuesday night’s clash. Hellebuyck is coming off a big win over the Toronto Maple Leafs on Sunday night. He posted his first career shutout with New Jersey in a big 4-0 win over the Maple Leafs. After the game, he reacted to the news of his benching for Tuesday night. “I’m disappointed, but I understand. Selfishly, I want to play. But when you’re looking at what’s best for the team, I understand where they’re coming from… It’s out of my hands,” the Devils star said, via Sportsnet. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Hellebuyck was asked about his desire to play against Winnipeg. The former Hart Trophy winner explained that he wanted to take that game head-on, even if Jets fans would provide a more hostile environment than he’s used to in Winnipeg. “I love Winnipeg. Playing there again, facing the music, seeing the reaction. It’d be nice,” the Devils star explained. The Devils have provided a couple of reasons as to why he will sit against Winnipeg. General manager Sunny Mehta said in a statement that it came down to the team’s expected win probability for this contest. Head coach Sheldon Keefe pointed to the veteran netminder’s workload . Unfortunately, fans won’t be able to unleash their emotions on Hellebuyck as he plays against their team. However, the former NHL MVP will be there in person to soak up all the noise. The Devils will face the Jets on Tuesday night in Winnipeg, with the game set to begin at 7 p.m. Eastern Time. Related: Devils make stunning Connor Hellebuyck decision before Jets clash Related: Matthew Schaefer, Luke Hughes throwdown during Islanders-Devils NHL clash

item.title: Mitch Albom: Lions won't have many easy wins. But does it matter?
item.description: Dan Campbell knew what this was by halftime. He barked it into the CBS cameras. “We gotta calm down … and then we GOTTA GO! We can’t be messing around!” Exactly. When playing a team that is 1-6, a good team often finds itself inexplicably fumbling and bumbling. It’s like when you can’t get that first piece of plastic to peel off the box. You start normal, then you try your fingernails, then you get frustrated, and you wind up screaming to yourself, “Why is this so damn hard?” That was the Detroit Lions for much of Sunday’s game in Miami against the low-win but high-effort Dolphins . Detroit’s first drive used up nearly seven minutes but ended with a sack of Jared Goff on third-and-goal. A field goal had to suffice. Their second drive ended in an interception, when Goff was pressured and a defender hit his arm as he tried to pass. Their third drive ended with a punt. Their fourth drive, after starting with great field position, fizzled when Jahmyr Gibbs was yanked down twice in a row for thre- yard losses and Goff was pressured into a scramble. Another field goal. The NFL’s highest-flying offense was hovering very close to the ground. Fortunately, Miami couldn’t take advantage. They punted twice, notched a field goal, and wasted an 11-play drive with a doink off the uprights by their kicker, Zane Gonzalez. Halftime ended at Lions 6, Miami 3. Which is what led Campbell to his “we can’t be messing around” critique, which I’m sure he delivered in the locker room with a fervor that would have scared the average TV viewer. And eventually, they did stop messing around. And they finally brought home a 19-9 win that may have certain critics attacking them for, well, not being able to get the plastic off a box faster than that. They’d be wrong. [ LIVE REACTIONS: Make the "Freep Sports Show" your go-to Detroit/Michigan sports podcast, available anywhere you listen ( Apple or Spotify ). Join us live on YouTube after every Lions game. ] Settling in Remember, this is a team coming off an emotional injury to one of their most beloved and important players, linebacker Jack Campbell. It swirled around practice all week. When one football player sees another football player face down and not moving, it stays with them − believe me. Dealing with Campbell’s health uncertainly, then getting a positive message from him midweek, then having to focus on an opponent that should be easy to beat ... well, all that is a perfect recipe for the old trap game, where you go home shaking your head saying, “How did we lose to them ?” That didn’t happen Sunday against the Dolphins, and the Lions first deserve credit for that. Four plays into the second half, safety Chuck Clark snagged a Malik Willis pass and turned into a running back, cutting angles and using blocks. He returned the ball 34 yards to the Miami 26. For a maligned secondary, it was a sweet moment and a turnaround, one that invoked Campbell’s “no more messing around.” LIONS GRADES: High marks for defense in emotional

item.title: Justin Gaethje vs. Ilia Topuria 2 Will Never Happen, Ali Abdelaziz Makes Bold Claim
item.description: One of the biggest talking points in MMA right now is who Justin Gaethje will face once he recovers from the injuries he sustained at UFC Freedom 250 . “The Highlight” enjoyed a massive night on June 14, battering Ilia Topuria before forcing the Spaniard to quit on his stool at the end of the fourth round. Although Gaethje initially ruled out an immediate rematch, his stance has seemingly softened since then. However, the lightweight champion is yet to make a decision about his future and remains uncertain about whether he wants to compete again. Meanwhile, Topuria has hinted at an April 2027 return in his first interview since the White House event. He also recently asked his Instagram followers whether they would rather see him run it back with Gaethje or settle his long-running rivalry with Paddy Pimblett. The results heavily favored a rematch with Gaethje. However, Ali Abdelaziz believes fans shouldn’t get their hopes up , as he doesn’t see that fight happening. Ali Abdelaziz Admits Ilia Topuria’s Recent Career Revelation Was True Topuria recently took to Instagram to ask his followers which opponent they wanted to see him face next. After 24 hours, Gaethje came out on top, receiving 474,000 votes compared to Pimblett’s 385,000. However, just a day after the results came in, Gaethje’s manager made it clear that his client has no interest in sharing the Octagon with the Spaniard again. Abdelaziz took to X and wrote, “This rematch will never happen. I agree with him – his brother saved his life.” The comment was a reference to Topuria recently revealing that his brother, Aleksandre, saved both his fighting career and his life by stepping in and calling the fight at the end of Round 4 on June 14. Abdelaziz further explained why he believes Gaethje won’t entertain a second meeting with the former champion. He added, “It’s very hard to come back from the trauma of a fight like that. I’ve seen Justin do this to many people, and coming back wasn’t easy for them. Wishing him the best of luck.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by HOME OF FIGHT (@homeoffight) ALSO READ: Shavkat Rakhmonov Pushes Back Against Fresh Knee Injury Reports, Hints at UFC Return in Early 2027 It certainly sounds like Gaethje’s camp has little interest in revisiting the matchup. However, the lightweight champion won’t be short of potential opponents if he decides to return. Arman Tsarukyan is waiting in the wings for another shot at UFC gold after finishing Mauricio Ruffy at UFC 331. The victory was so convincing that even Gaethje acknowledged him as the division’s true No. 1 contender. Alexander Volkanovski has also floated the idea of facing Gaethje for the lightweight title in what could be a retirement fight for both the veterans. With several intriguing options on the table, Gaethje’s next move remains uncertain. item.title: 19 Years Later, Avatar’s Most Terrifying Episode Changed the Franchise Forever
item.description: For much of Avatar: The Last Airbender , waterbending seems like the most limited of the four elements for one practical reason: Its wielders need access to water. Firebenders generate their own flames. Earth is everywhere, and air is even more readily accessible. On her adventure with Aang, Katara is almost never separated from her water skin for this very reason. A waterbender in the desert is about as useful as a badgermole cub in a swimming pool.

item.title: Boston Celtics rally to stomp Milwaukee Bucks, 117-97, and improve to 8-2
item.description: Effort is difficult to quantify in the NBA. However, there are a few areas of the game that can occasionally reveal its presence. For an example of this phenomenon during the Boston Celtics' 117-97 win over the Milwaukee Bucks on Sunday night, look no further than the final offensive rebound totals. The C's corralled a whopping 20 offensive boards at Fiserv Forum in Milwaukee while the Bucks only grabbed 9. Such a significant disparity suggests that the Celtics, who trailed 20-6 about halfway through the first quarter, stepped up their effort when things didn't immediately go their way. In fact, 4 of Boston's 6 offensive rebounds in the first frame occurred after it went down double digits. Meanwhile, Milwaukee had 0 offensive rebounds in that same span, and just 1 in the entire first quarter. Because the Celtics dominated the glass, they ended up with 16 more field goal attempts than the Bucks. From there, it's a math game, as Boston converted on 45 of its 95 shots (47.4 percent from the field) while Milwaukee hit 35 of its 79 shots (44.3 percent from the field). As for the rest of the margins, the Celtics garnered 12 steals — another effort-related stat — to the Bucks' 5 and prevailed in the points in the paint battle, 44-28. All of these numbers added up to the Celtics' third straight win and the Bucks' sixth straight loss. Before the now 8-2 Celtics face the 9-2 Philadelphia 76ers on Tuesday night in a highly-anticipated matchup, let's take a closer look at the most memorable moments from Boston's blowout victory captured in images below. Listen to "What have we learned about the Celtics two weeks into the NBA season?" on Spreaker. item.title: Yankees news: New York leads race for 21-year-old Japanese pitcher
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 29: A New York Yankees hat sits during batting practice prior to Game One of the American League Wild Card Series against the Boston Red Sox at Yankee Stadium on September 29, 2026 in the Bronx borough of New York City. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images Sports Hochi : The Yankees are reportedly setting their sights on 21-year-old Japanese right-hander Hironari Hiroike, who pitched at Keio University in Tokyo. The site called the Bombers ‘the most likely destination’ for the young and talented hurler, who had a 2.88 ERA and a strikeout rate of 11.52 in six games in the Tokyo Big6 Baseball League. With a mid-90s fastball that can reach 97 mph and multiple promising breaking balls, Hiroike wasn’t drafted in the NPB and is expected to sign a minor league deal with an MLB squad. FOX Sports | Rowan Kavner and Deesha Thosar : The offseason, or at least the first portion of it, is already underway. Kavner and Thosar went through each team’s biggest need and identified an infield bat as the Yankees’ most pressing one. “Outside of first base, there are a lot of questions about the offensive production of this infield. They need another reliable bat,” they said. Roundtable | Matthew Schmidt : Around the deadline, reports suggested the Yankees were interested in upgrading the catcher position. Ultimately, they chose to stick with Austin Wells as the primary guy behind the plate, but Schmidt wonders if they will revisit trade talks for Colorado Rockies backstop Hunter Goodman, who finished the 2026 campaign with 41 home runs and a 112 wRC+. He also explains why New York would be better off with Wells as the backup and Goodman or Ryan Jeffers starting. New York Yankees on SI | Jonna Perlinger The Yankees extended a qualifying offer to closer David Bednar, so there’s a good chance he takes it and stays on a one-year deal. He could also reject it and hit the free agent market, and Perlinger identified four potential landing spots for the big righty if he leaves the Bronx.

item.title: Bayern Munich News: Will Nick Woltemade eventually play for FC Bayern?; German club votes for name change; and MORE!
item.description: (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images) | Getty Images Never say never on Woltemade to Bayern (Sport Bild’s Christian Falk) Will Bayern Munich eventually throw Nick Woltemade a life preserver to help save his career? Sport Bild’s Christian Falk will not fully rule it out—it just will not happen any time soon: “I can say it’s not true that Bayern are concretely interested in Nick Woltemade at the moment. I won’t say that he’s categorically not an idea for the future. However, he has to perform. He has scored a few goals for Juventus, but most of these are penalties. He’s not in the starting XI in the league and it’s the same problem in the national team. Ultimately, we have to see more of the performances he was putting in during his peak at VfB Stuttgart. At the moment, he looks a shadow of the player we all saw and enjoyed in the Bundesliga. Of course, we have to emphasize that he’s young (24), he has talent and can play. Bayern Munich and him, they have history. So, never say never, but it’s not a definite move Bayern are making at this stage.” As Little Carmine said in The Sopranos , Woltemade’s career is at the precipice of an enormous crossroads. Newcastle United knows it messed up ( “What have we done?” ), Juventus does not seem to want to deal with the problem ( “Hey, we’ll give you a place to suit up, but we can’t fix you!” ), and now the attacker does not even have the German national team to fall back on. These are, indeed, sad days for the big German. LFC eyeing Verbruggen? (ESPN) Liverpool could be eyeing Brighton & Hove Albion goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen: “Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen has emerged as an option for Liverpool next summer, Football Insider reports. The 24-year-old has been a regular for the Seagulls in recent seasons, and several clubs are now monitoring his future. For the Reds, the interest comes during uncertainty over Alisson’s place at Anfield, with his contract expiring at the end of the season.” Verbruggen, of course, has been linked to Bayern Munich at various points.. Upamecano, Laimer named to Kicker’s BuLi Team of the Week (Kicker via @iMiaSanMia) Bayern Munich stars Dayot Upamecano and Konrad Laimer were rightfully named to Kicker’s Bundesliga Team of the Week: Dayot Upamecano (5th time) and Konrad Laimer (2nd time) in Kicker's Bundesliga Team of the Week pic.twitter.com/AWAJxKnD7K — Bayern & Germany (@iMiaSanMia) November 8, 2026 Lukeba dreaming of Barca? (ESPN) No way! A player has a dream to play for a big club in La Liga? Next man up for that is RB Leipzig defender Castello Lukeba: RB Leipzig centre-back Castello Lukeba had dreams of joining Barcelona, according to Sky Germany’s Philipp Hinze. The 23-year-old wants to make the next step in his career by joining a top club and earning a call-up to the France national team. item.title: Wayshawn Parker gets positive update after injury scare during Utah/BYU game
item.description: Rob Gray-Imagn Images Wayshawn Parker gets positive update after injury scare during Utah/BYU game appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Utah football lifted its record to 9-0 for the first time since 2008 by beating BYU 28-20 . But Utes fans received one scare involving star running back Wayshawn Parker. Which left fans hoping for good news nearly 24 hours after beating their fiercest rival. ESPN college football insider Pete Thamel dropped a deep, and promising, update there on Sunday evening. “He’s dealing with a bruise, and is expected to play on Saturday at No. 22 Arizona,” Thamel posted on the social media website X, formerly Twitter. “He was limited against BYU after appearing to injure himself on the opening drive, as he carried the ball only twice in the first half.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Parker settled for only 2.6 yards per carry against the nationally-ranked Cougars. He walked in averaging an astonishing 6.6 yards per carry. Parker also brought nine touchdowns in tow to the Holy War showdown. Turns out Utah didn’t need to rely heavily on Parker. Not with dual-threat quarterback Devon Dampier becoming a do-everything type. Dampier did more than throw a touchdown pass too. He rushed for multiple scores and even caught one deep pass on a trick play. So Utah will expect Parker to be healthy for the next big showdown on the unbeaten Utes’ schedule. Arizona escaped an upset attempt by TCU on Friday and will have Tucson rocking when Utah arrives. This heavyweight Big 12 Conference showdown surely will impact the College Football Playoff race. Especially if Arizona pulls off the upset of the Utes. Utah’s 9-0 starts brings this omen, however. Utah ended that 2008 season undefeated by trouncing a Nick Saban-led Alabama team in the Sugar Bowl. item.title: Kings crowd left in stunned silence after scary Keegan Murray fall vs. Heat
item.description: Credit: Dennis Lee-Imagn Images Kings crowd left in stunned silence after scary Keegan Murray fall vs. Heat appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . On Sunday night, Keegan Murray made his return for the Sacramento Kings in a tussle against the Miami Heat after a seven-game absence due to a left ankle injury. The Kings brought him back slowly, as Murray came off the bench behind De’Andre Hunter and didn’t check into the game until over four minutes had passed in the first quarter. It did not take long until Murray found himself near peril once more. With less than two minutes remaining in the first quarter, the recently-returned Kings forward leapt high near the rim before Heat big man Bobby Portis even attempted a shot. Murray then suffered a hard fall as Portis went underneath him, undercutting him and sending him crashing to the ground with a scary fall. The good news is that Murray was able to brace for impact, preventing him from landing on his head. Moreover, in a testament to his athleticism, he was able to roll a bit to his side to dampen the force of the blow he would take from landing on the hardwood. The Kings would immediately sub him out after this play. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Keegan Murray stayed in the Kings-Heat game despite this frightening fall 😳 pic.twitter.com/673gvOckOn — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 9, 2026 Murray did manage to stand on his own, and he did not have to go back to the locker room to get himself checked for a potential head injury. The Kings forward would return to the ballgame with 6:01 remaining in the second quarter, and he’s currently still playing for the team in the second half — dodging a major injury bullet. The 26-year-old forward has already gone through quite a few injury problems over the past few seasons. He played in just 23 games last season after ankle injuries plagued him all season long, and he already had to miss time earlier this year due to similar ankle issues. But with the Kings in a full-scale rebuild, Murray figures to play a huge role for the team moving forward as one of the team’s young bright spots. Related: Why Kings star Domantas Sabonis isn’t playing against Heat Related: Heat vs. Kings injury report: Keegan Murray upgraded

item.title: Pröschtli! Swiss Devils Lead the Way for Connor Hellebuyck’s 4-0 Shutout of Maple Leafs
item.description: TORONTO, CANADA - NOVEMBER 8: Timo Meier #28 of the New Jersey Devils scores against Anthony Stolarz #41 of the Toronto Maple Leafs during the second period at Scotiabank Arena on November 8, 2026 in Toronto, Canada. (Photo by Mark Blinch/NHLI via Getty Images) | NHLI via Getty Images For weeks, we’ve been watching as several Devils have been doing the little things that help win hockey games. Connor Brown has become a mongoose around the net, mixing it up with energy in close and being rewarded with goals. Cody Glass has been forechecking like a machine, forcing opposing defenders to move faster and causing turnovers that lead to Devils chances. Even Jack Hughes, the Devils’ most dangerous scoring threat, has been backchecking like his life depends on it. All over the ice, the Devils are doing things that don’t necessarily end up on the scoresheet, but are some of the most critical things that contribute to wins. Since the beginning of the season, the poster child for this kind of hockey has been Timo Meier. Timo has been using his big frame to cause havoc in front of opposing goalies, gotten his stick in passing lanes above the dots in the defensive zone, and taking the body on forwards in the neutral zone. That said, Timo has caught some flack this season for not getting on the scoresheet like some believe he should. He’s been firing away, but despite playing some damn good hockey, just hasn’t lit the lamp yet. Tonight, that changed. Timo busted out tonight, potting two goals to go along with goals by Nico and the utility knife, Connor Brown. If he can use this game as a launching pad to start racking up goals while still playing a complete game like he has been, he will be a real… Swiss army knife. I’m so sorry. I couldn’t help myself. Onto the game. First Period The game started relatively slowly with neither team registering a shot on goal through the first four minutes of play. Even almost 14 minutes into the game, each team had only taken three shots on the opposing netminder. For their part, the Devils’ shots to this point had largely been kept to outside the faceoff dots, with Anthony Stolarz handling the long-range pucks with relative ease. Same in the Devils’ end, where most shots came from the point, and Hellebuyck kicked out most rubber with little drama. Aside from a few weird bounces that led to shots in close at funky angles, everything was pretty even-keel throughout the opening period. Just a quiet beginning to the game. The Devils outshot the Leafs 7-4 in the first, but both teams go scoreless. We go into the locker room knotted at 0. Second Period The second period began much faster than the first, with the Devils looking particularly energetic. I mention it in a little more detail below, but Jesper Bratt had a strong move to the net that started from the right point. When a player can start his drive to the net from where some players tee-up point shots, you know he has a strong stride. In any event, Bratt’s move inside was

item.title: Vikings get no help in the NFC playoff picture Sunday
item.description: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-NOVEMBER 1: Head coach Kevin O'Connell of the Minnesota Vikings follows the play during the first half of an NFL football game between the Minnesota Vikings and the Detroit Lions in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Sunday, November 1, 2026 (Photo by Jorge Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings could have moved back into first place on Sunday with some help. They didn’t get it. The San Francisco 49ers shellacked the Raiders to stay in first place in the NFC. The Vikings will need a Monday night win to keep pace with San Fran. The rest of the NFC North did the Vikings no favors. The Packers and Lions both won their games. The Bears also won on Sunday night. In addition to the division race, that’s the entire wild card picture, too. The NFC North has four teams in the playoffs right now. Outside the current playoff spots, the Seattle Seahawks, Los Angeles Rams, and Dallas Cowboys all won, too. The pressure is on. NFC playoff picture after ‘Sunday Night Football’ 1. San Francisco 49ers (7-1) 2. Minnesota Vikings (6-1) Monday Night Football 3. New York Giants (5-2-1) 4. Carolina Panthers (3-5, 1-1 NFCS) 5. Chicago Bears (7-2) 6. Detroit Lions (6-2) 7. Green Bay Packers (6-3) 8. Seattle Seahawks (5-4, 2-1 NFCW) 9. Los Angeles Rams (5-4, 0-2 NFCW) 10. Dallas Cowboys (4-5) 11. New Orleans Saints (3-5) 12. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6, win over ATL, 3-3 NFC) 13. Atlanta Falcons (3-6, loss to TB, 3-3 NFC) 14. Arizona Cardinals (3-6, 2-5 NFC) 15. Washington Commanders (2-5-1) 16. Philadelphia Eagles (2-7) If the Vikings lose, they fall behind the Bears in the NFC North and into a tie with the Lions at 6-2. Minnesota’s loss to the Lions would put Detroit ahead of them, too. Minnesota falls from second in the NFC to sixth with a loss.

For Williams, his limited turnovers have helped lead an elite Bears offense, emerging as a potential Super Bowl contender. Mayfield has also historically taken care of the football; despite playing through injuries in 2026, the veteran has at least been careful with his passes. But both former Heisman Trophy winners and No. 1 overall picks had an ugly showing on "Sunday Night Football," which wound up being a game full of turnovers. Mayfield and Williams combined for six interceptions — and it led to a wacky, back-and-forth game between the Bears and Buccaneers , which Chicago narrowly escaped with a 27-24 win. item.title: Buccaneers lose Antoine Winfield Jr. to concerning injury in SNF vs. Bears
item.description: Credit: Talia Sprague-Imagn Images Buccaneers lose Antoine Winfield Jr. to concerning injury in SNF vs. Bears appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Coach Todd Bowles’ Tampa Bay Buccaneers took on the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field with eyes on inching closer to the .500 mark on a day when an NFL broadcasting legend’s health became an issue. Emeka Egbuka’s injury status became a hot topic before the game while Antoine Winfield Jr.’s became one later on in the evening. Bears reporter Dan Wiederer of The Athletic broke the news that the Buccaneers’ star cornerback, Winfield Jr., suffered an ankle injury and was expected to miss the remainder of the game. Winfield Jr. was third on the Bucs with four tackles before the injury occurred, causing Bowles to get creative with his defensive rotations. Winfield Jr. has 20 tackles this season and is known as one of the NFL’s most alert and physical defensive backs, playing at a position of need for coach Bowles’ team. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Bucs fell behind 17-6 heading into halftime, but drew to within 17-13 on a two-yard Bucky Irving touchdown run in the third quarter. The Bears’ defense stepped up after that as they intercepted Bucs QB Baker Mayfield, turning defense into offense. Jaylon Johnson snagged a Mayfield pass and took it 33 yards to the house, followed by a Cairo Santos extra point to make the score 24-13 in favor of Chicago at Soldier Field. The Bucs’ defense managed a few big plays of its own, intercepting Caleb Williams twice and keeping the Bears from blowing the game wide open. Winfield Jr.’s injury continued to haunt Bowles and his players as they attempted to mount a comeback. Winfield Jr. is one of Tampa Bay’s cornerstones, and a player who inspires his teammates every week on the football field, whose durability is almost never in question. His loss stung, but Tampa Bay knew they needed to keep pushing as the Bears showed little sign of slowing. item.title: Election fever, Dangote Refinery to drive stock investors’ fortune at year end
item.description: By Peter Egwuatu The Nigerian stock market is projected to cross the N200 trillion market capitalisation by December 2026, while investors’ returns could exceed 57 per cent. Capital market analysts, who made the projections, said the anticipated listing of shares of Dangote Petroleum Refinery on the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX), coupled with improved investor confidence, strong corporate earnings, increased market liquidity and favourable macroeconomic developments, would provide further impetus for the equities market. They also projected that the NGX All-Share Index (ASI), the market’s major performance indicator, could close the year at about 280,000 points. However, some analysts have warned that profit-taking, election-related uncertainties and global economic developments could trigger intermittent volatility. But the analysts agreed that the concern over 2027 general election is around possible policy change adding that if there are no major adverse economic policy developments capable of undermining investor confidence the impact of the election would be less severe. Market performance so far A review of the market’s performance Year-to-Date, YtD, as at last week, showed that investors’ wealth had increased by N62.76 trillion, representing a 60.47 per cent appreciation. Market capitalisation, which measures the total value of listed equities, rose from N99.376 trillion at the beginning of the year to N162.134 trillion last week. Similarly, the NGX ASI appreciated by 60.5 per cent, rising from 155,613.03 points at the beginning of the year to 249,710.59 points. The impressive performance has been supported by relative stability in the foreign exchange market, renewed investor confidence, strong corporate earnings, easing inflation, improved liquidity in the financial system and the decision of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) to reduce the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) to 23 per cent. Analysts’ projections Speaking to Financial Vanguard on his projection for the year-end, Olatunde Amolegbe, immediate past President, Chartered Institute of Stockbrokers (CIS), and Managing Director, Arthur Stevens Asset Management Limited, said he remained cautiously optimistic about the equities market. He stated: “I remain cautiously optimistic about the Nigerian stock market for the rest of the year. My expectation is that the All-Share Index will deliver a full-year return of approximately 57.65%. “Although the market has recorded impressive gains so far, I expect some moderation in the coming weeks, as investors may take profits following the significant rally we have witnessed. We could also see some volatility as investors reposition their portfolios ahead of the new year. “On the positive side, relatively strong corporate earnings, improved investor confidence, increased domestic participation and ongoing economic reforms should continue to provide support for the market. item.title: Jordan Love makes feelings clear on Matt LaFleur’s decision to attack with 20-point lead
item.description: Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images Jordan Love has backed Matt LaFleur’s decision to keep attacking despite the Green Bay Packers holding a 20-point lead against the New England Patriots. The Packers were leading 34-14 late in the third quarter when they recovered a Patriots fumble. Rather than slow things down, LaFleur called for a deep pass that ended with Christian Watson scoring a 39-yard touchdown. Green Bay eventually secured a 45-27 victory, with Love throwing for 372 yards and three touchdowns as the Packers improved to 6-3. Jordan Love praises Matt LaFleur’s aggressive approach against New England Patriots Love was pleased that LaFleur refused to take his foot off the gas, particularly with the Patriots still capable of making a comeback. Speaking after the game, the quarterback said: “I love being aggressive. I love the way Matt [LaFleur] called the game tonight,” The touchdown pass to Watson stretched Green Bay’s advantage to 40-14. Love then added a successful two-point conversion himself, taking the lead to 28 points. LaFleur shared his quarterback’s approach, explaining that he did not believe the Packers could afford to relax against a talented opponent. He was also reluctant to take his starters out too early after recalling a previous game in Dallas that made him wary of allowing an opponent back into contention. Watson was one of the biggest beneficiaries of Green Bay’s attacking approach. He finished with seven receptions for a career-high 171 yards and a touchdown, while Matthew Golden recorded 10 catches for 164 yards and another score. According to NBC Sports , it was only the fourth time in Packers history that two receivers had recorded at least 150 receiving yards in the same game. Love also reached 100 career passing touchdowns with his first-quarter connection to Golden. However, the quarterback was already looking ahead after the impressive win. “The mindset has to be complete focus and preparation on Minnesota,” Love said, via Zach Jacobson of PackerDispatch.com. “You can’t let one game lull you to sleep; it’s a great performance tonight, but it’s about getting back to work.” The Packers now turn their attention to the Minnesota Vikings, with Love keen to ensure the victory over New England does not distract them from their NFC North ambitions. item.title: Bears 27, Buccaneers 24: Cairo Santos’ walk-off field goal seals sloppy win
item.description: (Talia Sprague-Imagn Images) CHICAGO — Nobody said it had to be pretty. The Bears took that to heart, turning the ball over five times in a 27-24 win against the Buccaneers that came down to a Cairo Santos 38-yard field goal as time expired. Quarterback Caleb Williams was responsible for four of the turnovers. He finished 22-for-37 passing for 279 yards, two touchdowns and four interceptions for a 61.5 passer rating. It was the first time Williams threw more than two interceptions in a regular-season game. Luther Burden III led all receivers with 97 yards on seven receptions. He exited the game in the fourth quarter after sustaining a blow to the head, resulting in a fumble. Burden was helped off by trainers. But the Bears’ big highlight — aside from Santos’ game-winner — came in the third quarter when cornerback Jaylon Johnson intercepted Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield and returned it 67 yards for a touchdown. The Bears head into the bye week at 7-2. The CHGO staff reacts to the Bears’ win … Adam Jahns : It was ugly. Very, very ugly. But it’s a win. The Bears looked like a team dealing with a bunch of injuries coming off a short week and an exhausting, emotional win over the defending Super Bowl champions on the road. But the entire defense deserves a game ball for what it did to offset four interceptions by quarterback Caleb Williams and Luther Burden’s lost fumble. Patrick Norton : An ugly win is still a win. The Bears didn’t look like the better team for a good chunk of the game after the first quarter. But two touchdowns in the first quarter — paired with Jaylon Johnson’s big pick-six — proved to be enough to defeat a scrappy Buccaneers team that simply wouldn’t go away. Joey Christopoulos : Caleb was working on a Jordan Shrug Game (Boiling Point). Then, lukewarm. In the end, Iceman Cometh. Hey NFL, wanna beat the Bears? Let them commit FIVE TURNOVERS. Bye week perfectly timed. Game ball, Jaylon Johnson.

item.title: LeBron James shines as Sixers down Bulls
item.description: Veteran superstar LeBron James scored 22 points with five assists, returning to form (Michael Reaves) LeBron James had his best game yet for the Philadelphia 76ers, who bounced back with a 127-121 win in Chicago on Sunday over a Bulls side that has now lost seven straight NBA games. Veteran superstar James scored 22 points -- his highest tally since joining the Sixers this summer -- in a return to form after a paltry eight points in Friday's disappointing loss to Cleveland. James also had five assists while Jaylen Brown top-scored with 29, Tyrese Maxey poured in 27 and Joel Embiid pulled down 10 rebounds. The star-studded Sixers have lost just twice so far this season, for their best start after 11 games since 2000. Philadelphia grabbed the lead early in the second quarter and never trailed from there, though a resilient Chicago pulled within two points in the closing stages. "We have a lot of guys that's been in situations, late-game situations, and we have a 'no panic' button," said James. "We understand that we got to get stops on this end, but if teams make a run, we understand how to be calm on the other end as well." The Bulls remain second-bottom of the Eastern Conference, ahead of only the Milwaukee Bucks -- the only team Chicago has beaten so far this campaign. They were without shooting guard Norman Powell, their second-leading scorer this season, who was placed on the injury report hours before tip-off with back discomfort. But Josh Giddey provided some hope with a double-double including 19 points and 15 assists. Meanwhile, James' former Los Angeles Lakers team overcame the absence of red-hot talisman Luka Doncic to beat the Detroit Pistons 121-116, and also move to 9-2. Doncic, who has been averaging more than 40 points per game this season, was left out with lower back tightness, the team announced. Austin Reaves stepped up, scoring 43 points, including two calm free throws in the final seconds to take the game beyond Detroit's reach. The Lakers never trailed but had to fight hard to retain a razor-thin lead for most of the fourth quarter. Daniss Jenkins led the Pistons' comeback attempt from the bench with 31 points, while Kevin Huerter added 24. Minnesota extended its fine start with a 115-100 win over struggling Utah. It was the Timberwolves' fourth straight win despite losing Anthony Edwards to injury. The Bucks suffered another loss, falling 117-97 to the Celtics, who rallied from an early 14-point deficit, while Dallas thumped Brooklyn 130-93. Giannis Antetokounmpo top-scored for Miami in a 114-108 win at Sacramento with 29 points and 14 rebounds, while the Los Angeles Clippers grabbed a rare win, defeating New Orleans 139-123. The Charlotte Hornets announced that forward Kon Knueppel will miss at least four weeks with a left hamstring strain, while guard Dennis Schroder is out for at least two weeks with the same injury. amz/js

item.title: Patrice Bergeron Shares Emotional Message to Former Bruins Teammates
item.description: BOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS - APRIL 30: Patrice Bergeron #37 of the Boston Bruins waves to fans before exiting the ice after Florida Panthers defeat the Bruins 4-3 in overtime of Game Seven of the First Round of the 2023 Stanley Cup Playoffs at TD Garden on April 30, 2023 in Boston, Massachusetts. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) Getty BOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS - APRIL 26: Patrice Bergeron #37 of the Boston Bruins looks on against the Florida Panthers during the first period in Game Five of the First Round of the 2023 Stanley Cup Playoffs at TD Garden on April 26, 2023 in Boston, Massachusetts. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) Getty A As part of the Hockey Hall of Fame’s Class of 2026, longtime Boston Bruins forward Patrice Bergeron was among the players selected to be forever enshrined in hockey immortality in Toronto. One of the greatest players in Bruins history, Bergeron was also known for his humble nature despite his elite defensive skills and status as one of the NHL’s greatest two-way forwards. He won numerous individual accolades throughout his career and helped the Bruins win the Stanley Cup in 2011, while also making two additional Stanley Cup Final appearances in 2013 and 2019. During the 2026 Induction weekend in Toronto, Bergeron interviewed with NHL Insider James Duthie to talk about his career, and he was sure to give credit to the organization and his former teammates for helping him along in his Hall of Fame journey. Boston Bruins Icon Patrice Bergeron Remained As Humble As Ever Getty BOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS – APRIL 26: Patrice Bergeron #37 of the Boston Bruins looks on against the Florida Panthers during the first period in Game Five of the First Round of the 2023 Stanley Cup Playoffs at TD Garden on April 26, 2023 in Boston, Massachusetts. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) While interviewing with Duthie, Bergeron was sure to credit his family, friends, and former teammates for helping to make his Hall of Fame induction possible. “It means a lot, but it also means a lot to share it with family and friends,” Bergeron said. “But of course, my teammates and the organization. The Bruins have been so loyal to me in my career, and you can never get this accomplishment alone. To me, I guess it’s a reflection of everyone that has helped me a long the way and sacrificed so much for me to be in this position. I’m very humbled and grateful, and obviously, a huge honor.” When asked if he always possessed natural leadership traits, Bergeron said that he felt it’s part of his makeup, but also credited the numerous Bruins legends that were routinely around the organization, along with a few of his former on-ice teammates in Zdeno Chara and Mark Recchi. “I think it’s a little bit of both. You want to be yourself, and you want to speak from the heart and lead by example,” he said. “I guess that was always in me I guess in a way, but also, you learn from a lot of guys. I was lucky to play in an organization with so much history and so many great

item.title: Mahomes overcomes injury scare in Chiefs win as Burrow shines in Madrid
item.description: Kansas City quarterback Patrick Mahomes suffered a right elbow injury and was sacked and fumbled in the second quarter but rallied to spark the Chiefs to an NFL victory over the New York Jets (Amy Kontras) Three-time Super Bowl champion Patrick Mahomes overcame an injury scare to lift Kansas City over the New York Jets on Sunday while Joe Burrow sparked Cincinnati to victory over Atlanta in Madrid. Two-time NFL Most Valuable Player Mahomes completed 23-of-31 passes for 242 yards and two touchdowns in the Chiefs' 35-12 triumph over the Jets. Burrow completed 24-of-29 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns and ran for another score in Cincinnati's 34-17 victory, the Bengals' fourth triumph in a row. At Kansas City, Mahomes suffered a right elbow injury and lost a fumble in the second quarter after being sacked by Jets rookie defender David Bailey, but his 120 passing yards and two touchdown throws gave the Chiefs a 14-12 halftime lead. Mahomes directed touchdown drives of 60 and 82 yards in the third quarter and 57 yards in the fourth and said the elbow was not a factor "once I got it warmed up a little bit." "It's doing good," Mahomes said of his right elbow. "It's part of playing football. You get hit, you've got to bounce back and we were able to get it loosened back up and we went back out there and played. "A couple of errant throws early in the second half. My guys rallied behind me. They ran the ball well in the second half. My offensive line did a great job protecting me and then I threw when I needed to." Kenneth Walker ran 18 times for 102 yards and a touchdown and caught four passes for 41 yards and two touchdowns for the Chiefs (6-2). The Bengals improved to 6-2, level with idle Pittsburgh atop the AFC North division ahead of their showdown next week. "The sky is the limit when we play like this. This is how we need to attack every game going forward," said wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase, who made 10 catches for 155 yards and a touchdown. "Intense impact," Burrow said of Chase. "He was unbelievable." Burrow leads the NFL with 23 touchdowns. "He does a good job getting out of the pocket and making scramble plays, keeping the play alive," Chase said. "That's why he's one of the best." The Denver Broncos improved to 7-2 with their fifth consecutive win as Bo Nix threw for 237 yards and two touchdowns in a 26-21 triumph at Carolina. - Niners reach 7-1 - San Francisco improved to an NFL-best 7-1 with a 38-17 home victory over the Las Vegas Raiders as Brock Purdy threw for two touchdowns and ran for another. item.description: Nov 8, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Bears defensive end Austin Booker (94) sacks Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield (6) in the second half at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Talia Sprague-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Tampa Bay Buccaneers took the primetime stage in week nine— Sunday Night Football on NBC. Not only would Cris Collinsworth be in the booth for the Buccaneers’ game but the team would take the field officially leading the NFC South. The first place Tampa Bay Bucs have dug themselves, with help, all the way out of the 0-4 early season hole they dug themselves into. Week nine would be the team’s first chance to put some distance between themselves and their NFC South rivals, will Tampa Bay rise to the occasion or will they falter in the spotlight? First Quarter: Sunday night’s first drive was Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams versus Todd Bowles and his defense. Ben Johnson versus most would be a mismatch and in the game’s opening drive that looked to be the case as Tampa Bay fans had to watch Chicago coast down the field and into Tampa Bay’s end zone for ten first score of the game. Early concerns for Todd Bowles may stem, not only from the results of the drive (seven points allowed), but also from the fact that Caleb Williams consistently broke outside of the pocket without any noticeable restriction. 7-0, Bears. No glove for Baker Mayfield and no first downs either, though the Bucs’ quarterback did eclipse his completion total from a week ago on the Tampa’s opening drive the net result was a three-and-out. Chicago’s next drive started with more first downs than Bucs had earned the game thus far and finished in the end zone once again. 14-0, Chicago. The Buccaneers’ first six snaps all went to Bucky Irving before Zac Robinson remembered other players play for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers— The other player targeted? Cade Otton. Mayfield’s incomplete pass to Cade Otton set up the game’s first dose of Mayfield magic. Third and long and Baker Mayfield scrambled his way around the pocket buying time before eventually directing Kenny Gainwell downfield for a 44 yard gain. Second Quarter: The Bucs’ drive would stall out and Todd Bowles would opt for a conservative approach to surprise of the fanbase, kicking a short field goal. 14-3, Bears. Not much changed for Todd Bowles’ defense on the next Chicago drive, easy completions, no contain on the quarterback, and wide open receivers on most every play. The bleeding was finally stopped by a flagrant mistake when Chicago Bears’ rookie Zavion Thomas got frustrated and punched Jacob Parrish, pushed the Bears’ offense back 15 yards backwards. The ensuing play, Tykee Smith ruined the Caleb Williams showcase with a beautiful read undercutting a Williams throw to the end zone for for an interception. item.title: 4 Huge Takeaways After Reaves Leads Shorthanded Lakers Past Pistons
item.description: Mandatory Credit: David Gonzales-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Lakers entered Sunday night’s matchup as one of the top teams in the West with arguably the most in-form player in the league leading them . With Luka Doncic sidelined, concerns about L.A.’s chances of beating the Detroit Pistons seemed justified. Surprisingly, the Lakers dispelled all of these doubts. With a 121-116 win, the Los Angeles Lakers improved to 9-2 on the season, placing first in the West while notching their fifth consecutive win. While Doncic’s absence was undoubtedly a factor, Lakers’ star Austin Reaves showed exactly what he is capable of . From establishing a 26-point lead early in the game to defending against the Pistons’ furious comeback charge, the Purple and Gold displayed remarkable tenacity and fortitude. Additionally, with a dominant 43-point outing to lead L.A. past Detroit, Reaves showed how deep the Lakers truly are this season. Reaves’ performance was undoubtedly the most noteworthy aspect of Sunday night’s outing. However, with several key developments accompanying this, examine four key takeaways from L.A.’s win over Detroit. Austin Reaves Can Thrive In Doncic’s Absence The last few seasons have really seen Austin Reaves transform into a star-caliber player. With some spectacular offensive displays early last season as well, Reaves has demonstrated his ability to be a reliable scoring option. Despite this, there appear to be many who doubt it . After facing some early-season struggles , especially in light of his sizable contract extension, these comments would seem justified. Still, the 28-year-old proved naysayers wrong with his season-high scoring night against the Pistons. Needless to say, this is an extremely positive sign for the Lakers, who can be over-reliant on Doncic for creation. While Reaves lacks his running mate’s passing and playmaking ability, Sunday night’s display showed that he can certainly compensate for it with his scoring. With 43 points, five rebounds, and four assists on 14-27 FG and 4-6 3PT FG, Reaves had it going from everywhere. With some timely three-pointers in the fourth quarter, even while facing some tough defense, the guard showed exactly why he earned the Purple and Gold’s trust. Walker Kessler Needs More Offensive Involvement Walker Kessler has arguably been one of the most consistent performers for the Lakers this season outside of Luka Doncic. Having established himself as an elite big man, Kessler continues to dominate as a defensive anchor and a rebounder. Unfortunately, there are some issues that may demand some attention. On Sunday night, Kessler notched another double-double of 12 points, 16 rebounds, one steal, and three blocks, showcasing his overall involvement in the win. While his 16 rebounds and three blocks are eye-catching, his scoring on 5-10 shooting isn’t necessarily a positive sign. item.title: Vanguard, others organise Lagos gov debate: Our plans for housing, traffic, others — APC, ADC, NDC, PDP candidates
item.description: By Efe Onodjae LAGOS — THE Lagos State governorship candidates of the All Progressives Congress, APC, Dr Obafemi Hamzat; African Democratic Congress, ADC, Mr Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour; Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr Funso Doherty and Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, Mr Adedeji Doherty, yesterday, unveiled their development plans for housing, traffic congestion, transportation, security and infrastructure if elected in 2027. They presented their credentials, policy proposals and vision for the state ahead of the governorship election. The candidates spoke at a debate organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium, which comprises Vanguard Newspaper, Channels Television, TVC News, Punch Newspaper and The Cable. During the debate, the candidates outlined different approaches to addressing the developmental challenges facing Lagos. On the developmental challenges facing the state, the APC candidate, Dr Hamzat, emphasised continuity and expansion of existing infrastructure, while the ADC candidate, Mr Rhodes-Vivour, called for a departure from what he described as two decades of bad governance. In his remarks, the NDC candidate, Mr Doherty, questioned the political interests surrounding the state’s public transportation system, alleging that the failure to modernise the sector was deliberate. Taming traffic in Lagos On traffic congestion, Doherty alleged that the persistent gridlock in Lagos was being sustained by vested interests benefiting from the existing chaotic public transportation system. He argued that the state’s traffic problems were not simply the result of inadequate infrastructure but also reflected poor management of existing roads and the failure to modernise public transportation. The NDC candidate also alluded to the informal transport network popularly associated with agberos, arguing that the interests surrounding the system had made its modernisation politically difficult. He said: “Lagos continues to rely on dilapidated commercial buses operating chaotically, contributing to gridlock and making commuting difficult for residents. “Our public transportation system is not modernised. Thousands of rickety buses are moving around. We must ask ourselves: are these what our people deserve? Why has it taken so long to modernise public transportation? “In my opinion, the lack of modern transportation is not by accident. There are vested interests in operating the bus system the way it is. Many of us understand the agbero system; there is an ecosystem around it, and there is no political will to deal with that problem.” “We would modernise public transportation because we would be elected by the people and not by the agbero network,” he added. Hamzat, on his part, proposed expanding the state’s Bus Rapid Transit, BRT, system from about 1,000 buses to 4,000, with a target of transporting one million passengers daily. “The plan would involve deploying Compressed Natural Gas, CNG, buses and creating dedicated BRT corridors across major routes. item.title: FSU soccer loses to Virginia in ACC Tournament
item.description: No. 10 Florida State women’s soccer fell 3-0 to No. 14 Virginia on Sunday night in Tallahassee, ending its run in the ACC Tournament in the first round. With the loss, Florida State fell to 9-4-3 on the season, dropping its second straight game. Florida State’s starting 11 included Ryder Ajeto, Wrianna Hudson, Shaneil Buckley, Joelle Jung, Peyton McGovern, Nawreen Ahmad, Tanner Strickland, Bridget Mutipula, Janet Okeke, Grace Hoytink and Kate Ockene. At 13:25, Hudson’s shot was saved by Virginia goalkeeper Victoria Safradin, and Hudson followed with another attempt 13 seconds later that went wide right. Buckley also sent a shot wide right at 14:36. At 19:57, Ockene came up with another save, this time on Giovana Canali. Florida State earned a corner kick at 30:10, and moments later at 30:49, Ashley Henderson put a shot on frame, but Safradin made the save. Virginia broke through at 38:09 when Allie Ross scored off an assist from Ella Carter, giving the Cavaliers a 1-0 lead. The Seminoles entered halftime trailing by one despite holding a 3-0 advantage in corner kicks. Virginia outshot Florida State 5-4 in the opening half, with each goalkeeper recording two saves. Virginia extended its lead early in the second half. At 51:24, Ockene saved a shot from Carter, but Canali was there to finish the rebound and make it 2-0. Florida State looked to respond. At 56:41, Okeke’s shot was saved by Safradin, and Hudson missed left at 58:23. Ockene kept the Seminoles within two with saves on Carter at 67:59 and Sarah Flammia at 71:51. At 76:34, Florida State earned a corner kick, but Virginia countered moments later at 76:47 as Canali scored her second goal of the night off an assist from Sophia Bradley, putting the Cavaliers ahead 3-0. The Seminoles continued pushing in the closing minutes. At 84:06, Hudson’s shot was saved by Safradin, and Florida State followed with back-to-back corner kicks that produced attempts from Hudson and Buckley, but neither found the net. Virginia finished with 12 shots, including nine on goal, while Florida State recorded 10 shots and four on goal. The Seminoles held a 7-2 advantage in corner kicks but were called offside five times. Ockene finished with six saves, while Hudson led Florida State with six shots, including two on goal. The Seminoles will now await their postseason fate as they look ahead to the NCAA Tournament.

item.description: Point guard Dedan Thomas Jr., pictured earlier this season, had another strong game Sunday night as UH beat Cal in the Lake Tahoe Classic. (Kevin M. Forward Chase McCarty had three 3-pointers - including two in the game's opening minutes - and 11 points in 12 minutes. McCarty was in the starting lineup after suffering a sprained left knee in the season-opening win against La Salle . item.title: Patriots DB Christian Gonzalez Reacts to Performance vs. Packers
item.description: New England Patriots defensive back Christian Gonzalez reacted to his bad day against the Green Bay Packers. Getty There were very few New England Patriots players who had good games on Sunday against the Green Bay Packers. However, arguably the worst performance on the field came from Pro Bowl cornerback Christian Gonzalez. PFF initially charted out the game for Gonzalez. According to them, he was targeted 11 times on 36 coverage snaps. On those 11 targets, he allowed 10 receptions. That was for 187 yards and 40 yards after the catch. He would allow a touchdown and only have one pass breakup. By no means was Gonzalez the sole reason why the Patriots lost 45-27. However, when the player you paid $135 million, making him the highest-paid player at his position, performs like that, it’s almost impossible to overcome mistakes by other players. New England Patriots DB Christian Gonzalez on His Performance Following the game, Patriots DB Christian Gonzalez knew how poorly he performed. There was never any avoiding it, and he admitted how poorly he played in the loss. “They got the best of me today … I had a bad game,” Gonzalez said . “I’m not shaken up by it. I’m not too worried about it. I’ll move on and be ready next week.” Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel wasn’t afraid to call out Gonzalez either. He publicly shared what he thought of the performance, and he also made it clear that it’s hard to expect the team to win without one of its best players performing to their standard. “When your best players don’t play good, you don’t have much of a chance in this league,” Vrabel said . Gonzalez previously missed time this season with a shoulder injury that he suffered back in Week 3. That cost him a couple of games. “I mean, they did a good job,” Gonzalez said . “He came out and ran good routes. Ran the routes they had in the gameplan and Jordan Love was able to get him the ball. I just gotta be able to finish and make those plays. I’m right there, I just gotta make those plays. I mean, it’s not the end of the world. I had a bad game. I’m not shaken up by it, I’m not too worried about it. I’ll move on and be ready for next week.” Patriots DB Christian Gonzalez on the Defensive Gameplan It doesn’t take a football genius to see that the gameplan didn’t work on defense for the Patriots. 45 points is the most the Patriots have allowed in a regular season game in 33 years. It’s also the most points they’ve allowed at home since 1970. Gonzalez addressed that gameplan after the game. However, as he explained, things went wrong when he couldn’t take away the X for the Packers. “The plan to stop the X plays I mean was just — just, like, playing our defense,” Gonzalez said . “There’s things that go into it… I can’t fall on a go route. I can’t turn and get tripped up. The defense is counting on me to hold down the backside, hold down everything else just like we have been. I mean, just stopping it. I mean, that was just the plan. item.title: Blackhawks Sticking With Blashill & Staff Despite Disastrous Start
item.description: Chicago Blackhawks general manager Kyle Davidson is scheduled to speak with the media Wednesday afternoon, but isn’t expected to discuss any changes involving Jeff Blashill and the coaching staff. According to team sources, Blashill will remain the Blackhawks head coach despite a disastrous 4-13-1 start to the 2026-27 regular season, with the club currently riding a six-game losing streak. Assistant coaches Anders Sorensen, Michael Peca , and Mike Vellucci are also safe for now. BREAKING: The Blackhawks will not make a coaching change and Jeff Blashill will remain their head coach ⤵️ https://t.co/JQokCEmojF — Scott Powers (@ByScottPowers) November 8, 2026 The Blackhawks have fallen remarkably short of the preseason expectations through 18 games, with only four wins and the NHL’s second-worst points percentage. With hopes of at least competing for a Stanley Cup Playoff spot in Year 5 of Davidson’s rebuild, being ranked towards the bottom of the league in every major statistical category is beyond disappointing. Goals scored per game? They’re 31st among 32 teams. Goals against per game? 31st. Shots on goal per game? 31st. 5v5 shot attempts per game? Dead-last. And it’s not just the numbers suggesting the Blackhawks have been downright terrible. The eye test backs it up plenty, with TNT analyst Paul Bissonnette hitting the nail on the head last Wednesday while breaking down the tape against the Florida Panthers. Bissonnette blasted the Blackhawks on national television, calling them a “soft” team and describing their timid brand of hockey as “Mickey Mouse” and “AHL-level”. The former NHL enforcer told no lies, with the standard set far too low for Chicago. Biz was very blunt about the Hawks: "I see a soft team… they don't really do anything well" 😳 Then broke down their troubles with the help of the whiteboard pic.twitter.com/IWasxvqECJ — NHLonTNT (@NHL_On_TNT) November 5, 2026 Then, just four nights later, the Blackhawks were embarrassed once again, getting pounded 9-2 by the defending champion Carolina Hurricanes on Saturday night en route to a sixth straight loss. It also marked the team’s ninth consecutive road loss to start the season, with a 0-8-1 record. The debacle in Carolina capped off a 0-3-0 Southeast road trip, with the Hawks getting outscored 18-6. Now back in Chicago with four days off before returning to action, the timing seemed right for Davidson and/or chairman Danny Wirtz to make a significant change, but it hasn’t happened yet. Ultimately, the Blackhawks elected not to go that route with Blashill right now, although it seems inevitable eventually, barring a drastic turnaround. Instead, the coaching staff and management reportedly got together on Sunday to discuss potential adjustments and changes moving forward. Some of those changes could become clearer when the team returns to the ice for practice on Monday morning. One has already been revealed, as backup goaltender Arvid Soderblom was placed on waivers Sunday. The Blackhawks
